title: Low Power Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Architecture by Sparsely Connected Spiking Neural Networks for Edge Applications
summary: This 2026-08-02 article proposes a sparse spike-aware FPGA architecture using LIF neurons and pruning to reduce overhead in spiking neural networks. Evaluated on the Iris dataset, it achieved 93.3% classification accuracy with 587 logic cells and 3.5 W power consumption. The work addresses hardware efficiency for edge computing applications.
tldr: A 2026 FPGA architecture paper demonstrates low-power spiking neural networks achieving high accuracy on the Iris dataset via pruning-aware event-driven computation.
sourceName: Journal of Low Power Electronics and Applications
evidence: In this work, we propose a sparse spike-aware and weight pruning FPGA architecture based on LIF neurons that minimizes spike activity and synaptic operations through pruning-aware event-driven computation.

Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed architecture achieved an overall classification accuracy of 93.3% while maintaining low hardware resource utilization and reduced power consumption.
